recentItems.title: Labour Party Conference: Burnham pledges change
recentItems.description:
Andy Burnham used his conference speech to pitch himself to the people and his party as the man to reset and rewire politics. 

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

Driven by the experience of losing his father he asked Brits to back a National Care Service, in part funded by ending the triple lock on pensions as we know it, and adjusting the link to average earnings from year on year to over time. Pensions would still rise, but not as much. 
Admitting he may pay a political price he insisted somebody had to take on the big decisions. 

He declared Brexit has caused ‘more harm than good’ and intends to look at a new deal with Europe with all options including rejoining on the table. 

He arrived looking like he was relishing it, but on stage he was, for a moment, engulfed by the emotion of talking about his father  

Is it the leadership Britain needs or, as one union boss has warned, electoral suicide?

recentItems.title: PM announces National Care Service Plans
recentItems.description:
Andy Burnham has announced plans for a National Care Service which would be free at the point of use, in his speech at the Labour Party conference.

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

The Prime Minister said the plans, which will be put to voters in the next election, would be paid for by adjusting the pension triple lock, which guarantees how much the state pension increases annually.

He referenced his personal experiences of both his grandmother and his father in care homes, and apologised to care workers for politicians letting them down for “so long”.
